topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the learning objectives regarding cancer etiology and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Biological Nature of Cancer and Sources of Cellular Mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by a combination of endogenous cellular errors, inherited traits, and permissive microenvironments.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Patterns in Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore common environmental exposures and the epidemiological evidence showing how geographical and lifestyle factors influence cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic pathogens contribute to malignancy, illustrated through the multi-factorial etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Radiation-Induced Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms through which radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical carcinogens damage DNA directly or via host metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate tumor initiators from non-mutagenic promoters and explain how chronic inflammation and host tissue proliferation status enable malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for Determining Carcinogenicity and Assessing Exposure Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, in vitro, and risk-assessment frameworks used to evaluate whether environmental agents cause cancer.
